q1.question: What do I get out of the box?
q1.answer: A full-stack app with React 19, Hono API, your own Postgres database, auth, billing, file uploads, blog, docs, i18n, Kubernetes manifests, and Docker Compose for local dev.

q2.question: Can I modify or customize everything?
q2.answer: Yes. Every line is yours, generated once and yours to keep. No vendor lock-in, no runtime dependency on Vibecarbon.

q3.question: What cloud providers are supported?
q3.answer: Hetzner Cloud, DigitalOcean, Linode, Vultr, and Scaleway: the same CLI, the same lifecycle, the same test coverage. Mode support varies by provider. Hetzner and DigitalOcean run Compose, Kubernetes, and Kubernetes HA (a standby copy in a second region, kept ready to take over). Linode, Vultr, and Scaleway run Compose today. The provider is chosen per environment when you first deploy it, so another environment of the same app can use a different one.

q4.question: How does deployment work?
q4.answer: Run "vibecarbon deploy" and one command does the whole job: rents and configures a server in your own cloud account, installs your stack, turns on HTTPS (the browser padlock) automatically, and sets up scheduled backups. Once it is live, the same CLI handles scaling and restore, plus failover in the HA modes.

q5.question: Which setup do I need?
q5.answer: Pick by circumstance, not by size. Launch runs most production apps: one server in your own cloud account, automated SSL, automated backups, one-command restore. Supercharge is for absorbing traffic spikes: a cluster that adds workers under load and deploys with zero downtime. Fortify is for surviving a region outage: a live standby in a second region with one-command failover.

q6.question: How many projects can I create?
q6.answer: As many as you like. There are no keys and no per-project limits.

q7.question: Can I charge users or run a SaaS?
q7.answer: Yes. Vibecarbon and the code it generates are MIT licensed, so commercial use and client work are fine.

q8.question: What happens if Vibecarbon shuts down?
q8.answer: Nothing changes for your app. The generated code is MIT-licensed with zero runtime dependency on Vibecarbon; it's just a codebase you own outright. The CLI is MIT too. Your infrastructure runs in your own cloud account.

q9.question: Do I need DevOps experience to deploy?
q9.answer: No. The CLI handles provisioning, SSL, scaling, backups, and monitoring. You need an account with a supported provider, a domain, and SMTP credentials for email. That's it. All the Kubernetes manifests and Docker Compose files live in your project if you want to understand or customize what's being set up.

q10.question: I'm building with AI. What stops my agent from making a security mistake?
q10.answer: Guardrails your agent is required to follow, not asked to. Generated projects ship with security rules AI agents must obey: row-level security on every table (the database itself refusing to show one customer another customer's data), sign-in checks, and input validation. There's also a scanner that blocks secret keys from ever being committed, and confirmation gates on anything destructive. The architecture helps too: browser code, server code, and the database are three separate pieces, so an agent can't accidentally put a secret where the public can see it.

q11.question: What does it cost to run?
q11.answer: The software is MIT licensed, so there is nothing to pay Vibecarbon. You pay your own cloud bill, which depends on your provider and deploy mode.
